newsitem.title: USA: AT&T CFO Miller to leave at end of March.
newsitem.headline: AT&T CFO Miller to leave at end of March.

text.p: AT&T Corp said on Monday that Chief Financial Officer Richard Miller, 56, would leave the company at the end of March, following through on plans he made more than a year ago to pursue interests outside the industry.

"He told (AT&T chairman) Bob Allen over a year ago that he wanted to see through the restructuring and then pursue his own personal interests which have nothing to do with AT&T or this industry," AT&T spokesmen Jim Byrnes said.
Miller, joined AT&T as chief financial officer in August 1993, the company said.

Miller is one of a number of senior executives to leave AT&T in the last six months, but the company emphasised his departure was not prompted by other opportunities within the industry, nor was it the result of changes by AT&T itself.
In August Alex Mandl resigned as AT&T chief operating officer to head a wireless unit of Associated Group Inc.
In December Joseph Nacchio resigned as executive vice president of AT&T's consumer and small-business division to become chief executive of privately owned Qwest Communications Corp.

"Rick Miller has contributed immeasurably to AT&T over the last three and a half years, especially in the design and implementation of our restructuring and in the discipline he applied to its aggressive 15-month timetable," Allen said.

AT&T in August 1995 announced a split into three publicly traded companies: a core telecommunications concern retaining the AT&T name, the equipment company Lucent Technologies Inc and the computer company NCR Corp.
The split, which included the sale of financing unit AT&T Capital Corp, was completed on December 31.
The stock was hit hard after other senior management changes at the company and the succession to Allen as chairman and chief executive, analysts said
The company's stock fell sharply in October when AT&T named a relative unknown, John Walter, as chief operating officer and chief executive designate.
AT&T was 1/8 higher at 39-1/2 in trading on the New York Stock Exchange on Monday.
